title: Offline release and a separate billing incident

threads.title: Trailbook offline release
threads.scope: Ship and assess offline field capture in Trailbook, including local drafts, synchronization and rollout monitoring as one release.

threads.title: Trailbook duplicate-charge repair
threads.scope: Resolve a separately tracked duplicate-charge incident in Trailbook billing and verify reimbursements.

threads.title: Bedroom curtain installation
threads.scope: Fit blackout curtains to a bedroom window.

captures.text: Trailbook offline release scope: local field drafts plus reconnect synchronization ship together. Design, sync tests and rollout monitoring belong to this release.
captures.rationale: Explicit scope unites UI and synchronization work into one undertaking.

captures.text: Open a separate billing incident for Trailbook's duplicate subscription charges. Repair payment retries and reimburse affected test accounts; this is outside the offline release.
captures.rationale: The application is shared, but the incident is explicitly separate.

captures.text: Offline draft screen mockup: show 'Saved on this device' until Trailbook reconnects, then replace it with the server timestamp.
captures.rationale: The screen implements the offline release's draft behavior.

captures.text: Retry still doubles it. Check the queue.
captures.rationale: Retry and doubling could describe either sync records or charges; the object is missing.

captures.text: Blackout curtain rail needs brackets 12 cm from each end. Measure the bedroom lintel before drilling.
captures.rationale: A household installation has no supported link to software delivery.

captures.text: Offline reconnect test: one locally saved field observation produces two server records after retry. Billing is not exercised by this test.
captures.rationale: A duplicate-record defect belongs to the offline sync release.

captures.text: The 'Retry still doubles it' voice memo was recorded during the offline reconnect test described in the written log. I meant two field records, not payment charges.
captures.rationale: Explicitly identifies the earlier memo's object and project.

captures.text: Billing incident repair: reuse one payment-attempt identifier across retries. The reimbursement checklist remains with the duplicate-charge incident.
captures.rationale: Implementation and remediation continue the billing incident.

captures.text: Offline release demo after sync fix: a draft survives airplane mode and appears once after reconnect. The saved-state label changes after acknowledgment.
captures.rationale: Demonstrates the same release across UI and backend phases.

captures.text: Release coordination: deploy the offline sync fix Tuesday and the separately approved billing retry repair Thursday. Both touch the worker, so reserve separate rollback windows.
captures.rationale: An explicit coordination note spans two distinct changes.

captures.text: Offline release rollout review: no duplicate field records in the staged test cohort. Keep reconnect latency as the next observation for this release.
captures.rationale: Monitoring and review continue the release undertaking.

captures.text: Duplicate-charge incident closed: retry check passed and the reimbursement ledger reconciles. This closes billing remediation, not the offline rollout review.
captures.rationale: Closes the separately scoped billing incident.

events.reason: c07 identifies the memo as the offline reconnect test. Assign it to the offline release.

events.text: Offline draft screen mockup revised: show 'Saved on this device' until Trailbook receives a server acknowledgment, then display the server timestamp. A network connection alone is insufficient.

challenges: Shared application, queue and retry language are weak identity evidence.
UI design and server fixes can be phases of one explicit release.
A deployment coordination bridge does not combine an incident with a feature.
Specific clarification is required for an object-free fragment.
authorNotes: Trailbook and all data are fictional; no real accounts, code or logs are used. c07 describes the earlier recorded test, while c06 is its later imported written result, so capture order differs from event occurrence.
